title: AES-256 five-round truncated differential feasibility [WJ18]

target.description: Five AES-256 rounds with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted; fixed AES S-box and the genuine 256-bit master-key schedule. The explicit witness uses two consecutive round keys K2,K3.

setting.key_relation: Real standard AES-256 key schedule: two consecutive freely chosen 128-bit round subkeys can be extended backwards/forwards to a master key.
setting.key_population: Existence over standard AES-256 keys, not every fixed key.
setting.plaintext_model: Source differential/linear patterns and their quantified propagation, not chosen-plaintext attack queries.
assumptions: Real standard AES-256 key schedule: two consecutive freely chosen 128-bit round subkeys can be extended backwards/forwards to a master key.
setting.reference_model: Zero key-averaged probability means impossibility for every standard AES-256 master key. Positivity establishes existence of a compatible master key and input pair; never all patterns for each fixed key.

time.note: A structural statement, not an operational attack resource.

success.description: A quantified structural property, not attack success.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.4–5 Definitions3,6,7 (key-averaged probability and existential positivity); PDF pp.9–11 Theorem2 constructive five-round proof; PDF p.11 Property1 and Theorem3 (consecutive AES-256 round-key inversion).
evidence.interpretation: All12 primary PDF pages read independently. Nonzero probability signs visually checked; component equation printing issues are separately retained with their source-local resolutions.

limitations: Key-averaged support positivity is existential over keys and plaintext pairs, not positivity of every concrete differential or of every pattern under each fixed key.
The theorem concerns key-independent byte-activity truncation, not key-dependent subspace/integral distinguishers or the attackable round limit.

The paper explicitly constructs a five-round witness; its maximum-length statement is retained as the source claim. Reviewer finite checks do not exhaust all five-round inputs/keys or independently prove every longer interval.
Any chosen pair of consecutive128-bit AES-256 round keys extends to exactly one standard master key; this unrestricted pair-selection claim does not hold for AES-128 or AES-192.

property.statement: For every pair of nonzero byte-activity input and output patterns, the five-round truncated differential has positive probability after averaging over standard AES-256 master keys.
property.quantifier: For every nonzero input pattern P and nonzero output pattern Q, there exist a standard AES-256 master key K, concrete nonzero difference a with chi(a)=P, and an input x such that chi(E_K(x) XOR E_K(x XOR a))=Q. The key and input may depend on P,Q.
property.scope: Theorem3 standard AES-256 master-key model, explicit five-round construction with last MixColumns omitted. The source also states the maximum key-independent byte-truncated impossible-differential length is4; this is not a theorem on every fixed key or every concrete differential.

parameters.name: max_id_rounds
parameters.meaning: Source-stated upper bound for key-independent byte-truncated impossible differentials in the stated key model; the explicit support witness targets5 rounds.

validation.description: Complete independent raw-first read of all12 PDF pages. Reviewer-generated exhaustive inverse/S-box support checks, trace-hyperplane checks, finite simultaneous-offset witnesses, MixColumns support controls and AES-256 round-key inversion tests support individual proof steps; not exhaustive five-round AES support reproduction.
